quotes.citation: Haribhadra, འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། (Sphuṭārthā, Tengyur Toh. 3793) — the closing clause of his prose paraphrase of the Ornament's homage verse
quotes.why: The lemma this paragraph opens by quoting; note that both editions of Haribhadra in this archive read ཡུལ་ where the yig cha and every Tibetan commentator read ཡུམ་.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/TD03786_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན། (Tengyur Toh. 3786) — fourth line of the homage verse
quotes.why: The root line whose བཅས་ ("together with") Haribhadra rewrites as ཡོངས་སུ་བསྐོར་བ་ ("encircled by"); the whole paragraph is about that substitution.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 9 (TA)/TD03800_BCOM LDAN 'DAS MA SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN GYI 'GREL PA SHES RAB SGRON MA'I PHRENG BA ZHES BYA BA (Abisamayālaṃkāra Bhagavatī Prajñā Paramitopadeśa Śāstra Vr_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Buddhaśrījñāna, ཤེས་རབ་སྒྲོན་མའི་ཕྲེང་བ། (Prajñāpradīpāvalī, Tengyur Toh. 3800) — gloss on the homage verse
quotes.why: The Indian passage the paragraph cites as ཤེས་རབ་སྒྲོན་མེ: it names all three kinds of Ārya as the encirclers and the Perfection of Wisdom as 'their Mother'.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 2 (KHA)/TD03788_'PHAGS PA SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN GYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA'I RNAM PAR 'GREL PA ((Ārya) Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitopades_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Vimuktisena, ཉི་ཁྲི་རྣམ་འགྲེལ། (Vārttika, Tengyur Toh. 3788) — the homage verse as rendered in this commentary
quotes.why: The source of the paragraph's ཉི་ཁྲི་རྣམ་འགྲེལ citation: here ལྡན stands directly before ཡུམ, so it is the Mother who is 'endowed with' the assembly.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། — gloss on Haribhadra's homage, immediately after citing the ཤེས་རབ་སྒྲོན་མ
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's argument, which this paragraph condenses: Haribhadra agrees with the Vārttika, reads the root's བཅས/ལྡན as 'encircled', and so parts company with Śāntipa; the encircled one is the Mother.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། — continuation of the same gloss
quotes.why: The origin of the paragraph's ཡུམ་སྲས་ལ་གཙོ་འཁོར་གྱི་ཐ་སྙད, together with Tsongkhapa's dismissal of the rival 'Buddha as principal, others as retinue' reading.

quotes.citation: རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། — the whole of Gyaltsab Je's comment on this clause of Haribhadra
quotes.why: What the paragraph means by 'the Ornament of Essence says only this': Gyaltsab restates Haribhadra with བཞེད་དོན inserted and does not say who is encircled; his wording differs slightly from the yig cha's quotation of him.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་ཚིག་དོན་རབ་གསལ། — gloss on the same clause of Haribhadra
quotes.why: Panchen Sonam Drakpa resolves Gyaltsab's open wording the other way — Buddha principal, śrāvakas and bodhisattvas retinue — the very gloss Tsongkhapa called a pseudo-thesis. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 9 (TA)/TD03801_MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN GYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA'I 'GREL PA DAG LDAN ZHES BYA BA (Abisamayālaṃkāra Kārikā Vṛtti Śuddamati (Nāma))_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Ratnākaraśānti, དག་ལྡན། (Śuddhamatī, Tengyur Toh. 3801) — gloss on the homage verse
quotes.why: The 'Śāntipa' reading Tsongkhapa sets aside: the assembly goes with the Buddha, and the Mother is the mother of the Buddha-with-his-assembly. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 9 (TA)/TD03801_MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN GYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA'I 'GREL PA DAG LDAN ZHES BYA BA (Abisamayālaṃkāra Kārikā Vṛtti Śuddamati (Nāma))_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Ratnākaraśānti, དག་ལྡན། (Śuddhamatī, Tengyur Toh. 3801) — the objection and reply that follow
quotes.why: Ratnākaraśānti sees the difficulty in his own construal — does the wife of a man with a son become the son's wife? — and answers that ལྡན here means only 'together with'. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: Abhayākaragupta, གནད་ཀྱི་ཟླ་འོད། (Marmakaumudī) — gloss on the homage verse
quotes.why: A second Indian commentator construing the line as Ratnākaraśānti does — one of the 'and others' in Tsongkhapa's ཤཱནྟི་པ་སོགས. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — own-system definition of the Mother that is the object of the Ornament's homage
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own definition of the Mother, whose wording is exactly the reason clause of this paragraph. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — this text's own earlier outline of the root homage verse
quotes.why: Earlier in this same text, the fourth line of the root verse is already read as praise of the Mother of the four Āryas — the reading p99 now finds in Haribhadra. Found by direct search.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the division of Haribhadra's homage paraphrase, shortly before p99
quotes.why: The division that gives p99 its heading: 'praise of each knowledge's qualities' and then 'the condensed homage', of which p99 is the second. Found by reading the text.
